claims.text: Rapid quenching of nominal FeCoNiTi produces a dual-phase microstructure containing an fcc matrix and C14 Laves precipitates.
The C14 Laves phase enhances the coercivity of dual-phase FeCoNiTi.
The proposed coercivity enhancement does not result from an increase in the intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase.
The Ti-rich C14 phase and Fe/Co-rich fcc phase are strongly antiferromagnetically coupled across their interface.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling creates a magnetic dead layer at fcc/C14 boundaries.
The interfacial magnetic dead layer suppresses the net saturation magnetization of the fcc grains.
The fcc/C14 interfaces generate high local magnetic anisotropy.
The fcc/C14 interfaces act as effective domain-wall pinning sites.
At the interface, fcc magnetic moments align antiparallel to moments on the Ti sublattice of the C14 phase.
Antiparallel interfacial alignment lowers saturation magnetization through moment compensation.
C14-phase anisotropy and interfacial strain create energy barriers that impede domain-wall motion.
Domain-wall pinning increases coercivity despite the low intrinsic orbital moment of the fcc phase.
The dual-phase alloy will have a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
The dual-phase alloy will have lower saturation magnetization than a single-phase fcc alloy of the same composition.
A C14-dominant alloy will show a distinct magnetic transition near either 168 K or 214 K.
A C14-dominant alloy will show negligible coercivity enhancement relative to the dual-phase system.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys have coercivity capped at 100 Oe because of insufficient orbital moments and weak pinning.
The proposed coupling mechanism requires a coherent or semi-coherent fcc/C14 interface and may fail for fully incoherent or amorphous boundaries.
The coercivity enhancement may diminish above the Curie temperature of the C14 phase.
Spin-polarized DFT on a coherent fcc(111)/C14(0001) interface can test the sign and magnitude of interfacial exchange and determine the spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level.

contradictions.description: The stated measurement window extends only from 4 K to 400 K, yet it is said to track a transition near 1084 K; that transition cannot be directly measured within the specified range.
